research_question: How does AV active vehicle-hour penetration affect effective service capacity?
method_component: Exact vehicle-hour normalization; reconstructed HV sessions; full-horizon AVs; rolling sparse dispatch
experiment: 27-scenario factorial over q_A; profile; p_A plus all-HV and all-AV composition benchmarks
result: Marginal mean service fell from 0.7258 at q_A=.25 to 0.3924 at .75; peak service fell as queue pressure rose despite greater total available stock
discussion_implication: Nominal vehicle-hours and idle stock do not alone measure deployable capacity; penetration should be evaluated by service and expiration

research_question: How do passenger AV acceptance and assumed AV capability moderate fleet transition?
method_component: Scenario-level p_A with frozen order-level a_o_A; hard feasibility; profile-specific static/dynamic/speed suitability
experiment: Acceptance and C/M/A profile factors crossed with q_A in the 27-scenario factorial
result: Profile M acceptance gain rose from 0.0087 at q_A=.25 to 0.0477 at .75; C-to-A gain was 0.0330 at q_A=.75 and p_A=.70
discussion_implication: Acceptance coordination becomes more important in AV-heavy fleets; capability mitigates but does not guarantee one-for-one HV replacement

research_question: Can family-specific cumulative operational-envelope budgets control AV exposure while preserving service?
method_component: Separate static/dynamic/speed exceedance; cumulative Gamma constraints; sequential lexicographic assignment
experiment: STRICT; REFERENCE; and UNCONSTRAINED policies at q_A=.50; profile M; p_A=.70
result: REFERENCE lost 0.0007 service while reducing static exposure 9.6% and dynamic exposure 5.6% relative to UNCONSTRAINED
discussion_implication: Finite transparent family budgets can provide a tested middle position between zero-exposure and unconstrained operation
